findings.text: The code performs an independent upstream catalog fetch and owner selection before joining the FIFO at line 565, so the FIFO orders requests by completion of catalog resolution rather than by arrival at the router. A later request whose catalog fetch completes first can enter the gate ahead of an earlier request, while the plan and evidence state first-come, first-served without this qualifier; the current test spaces calls against a uniform local catalog and does not exercise out-of-order resolution.

The plan, evidence figure, and imas_ambix/agent/AGENTS.md state that health requests bypass the generation gate, but RouterApp accepts only GET /v1/models and the three POST routed paths; GET /health reaches the unsupported-path 404 at line 477. No added test names health, so the durable record promises a decode-free health path that the reviewed router does not serve or relay.

justifications.durability: the eight behavioral tests cover the binding width, FIFO under uniform resolution, timeout shape and header, waiter and streamer departure, runtime edits, decode-free catalog/count-token bypass, and nonzero publication, while the declared mutation proves the width test depends on the acquire. They do not pin router-arrival FIFO across reordered catalog lookups or the documented health path.
justifications.evidence: the run stores revision- and command-headed receipts for the 45-test gate, ruff, interpreter compatibility, document audits, three pre-repair refusals, baseline reproduction, and a discriminating negative control. I independently reran the three no-socket checks at decc190bc (3 passed in 2.18 seconds); the review sandbox forbids loopback binding, so its socket-backed failure is environmental and preserved separately rather than presented as a source failure.
justifications.fit: the gate is instantiated once per RouterApp, derives its operator file beside lane.json in the production CLI path, keeps the 2048 transport ceiling separate, and publishes counters without replacing engine counters. The admission point follows per-request catalog discovery, which weakens the unqualified FIFO contract, and invalid configuration reverts to defaults rather than retaining the last known-good setting.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all four explicitly tested section-7 behaviors plus catalog/count-token bypass and counters are implemented at the reviewed revision, with no deployment. The two qualifications are that FIFO is post-resolution rather than arrival-order and health is documented as bypassed but remains unsupported.
justifications.scope_discipline: all seven changed paths are inside the initial fence or the coordinator's explicit scope widening, commits are separated into tests, implementation, correction and evidence, and the worker did not perform the separately authorised router restart.
